title_en: 237-million-year-old fossils reveal a bizarre armored sea amphibian
title_zh: 2.37亿年前的化石揭示了一种奇怪的有盔甲的海洋两栖动物

paragraphs.en: A remarkable fossil discovery in China has revealed an ancient amphibian that lived entirely in the ocean, something no amphibian alive today is known to do. The unusual animal, named Gerrothorax maritimus , had a broad, flattened body protected by bony armor and was roughly the size of a giant salamander. Researchers believe it spent much of its life on the seafloor, waiting to ambush passing prey.
paragraphs.zh: 在中国的一项非凡化石发现揭示了一种完全生活在海洋中的远古两栖动物，而现今已知的两栖动物中没有任何一种被认为会这样做。这种不寻常的动物被命名为海生格罗托拉克斯（Gerrothorax maritimus），身体宽大扁平，由骨质甲壳保护，体型大约与巨型蝾螈相当。研究人员认为，它一生中大部分时间都待在海底，等待伏击经过的猎物。

paragraphs.en: The discovery comes from an international team at the University of California, Davis, Peking University, and the Geological Museum of Guizhou. Their findings, published in Nature Ecology & Evolution , are based on two exceptionally well-preserved skeletons dating back nearly 237 million years to the Late Triassic period.
paragraphs.zh: 这一发现来自加州大学戴维斯分校、北京大学和贵州省地质博物馆组成的一个国际团队。他们的研究成果发表在《自然·生态与演化》（Nature Ecology & Evolution）上，依据的是两具保存异常完好的骨架，可追溯至近2.37亿年前的晚三叠世。

paragraphs.en: "This area is part of an ecosystem that we've been looking at and trying to reconstruct," said study corresponding author Ryosuke Motani, a professor in the Department of Earth and Planetary Sciences at UC Davis. "We've been mostly studying marine reptiles and the fish from this place, but now we also have this amphibian, and it's a sort of very unusual member of the lineage."
paragraphs.zh: “这个区域是我们一直在观察并试图重建的生态系统的一部分，”该研究的通讯作者、加州大学戴维斯分校地球与行星科学系教授元井良辅（Ryosuke Motani）说。“我们此前主要研究这里的海洋爬行动物和鱼类，但现在我们也有了这种两栖动物，它是该谱系中一个非常不寻常的成员。”

paragraphs.en: The finding is especially surprising because amphibians are generally unable to survive in seawater. Among the more than 8,000 amphibian species living today, none are known to spend their entire lives in marine environments, and fewer than 2% have any ability to tolerate salt.
paragraphs.zh: 这一发现尤其令人惊讶，因为两栖动物通常无法在海水中生存。在现今超过8000种两栖动物中，已知没有任何一种终生生活在海洋环境中，而能够耐受盐分的不足2%。

paragraphs.en: Mammals, reptiles, and birds, by comparison, all include species that can live entirely at sea without relying on land for food or fresh water. Until this discovery, scientists had never identified convincing fossil evidence of an amphibian with the same ability.
paragraphs.zh: 相比之下，哺乳动物、爬行动物和鸟类中都包含可以完全在海洋中生活、不依赖陆地获取食物或淡水的物种。在这一发现之前，科学家从未找到令人信服的化石证据，证明两栖动物也具备同样的能力。

paragraphs.en: Gerrothorax maritimus measured nearly three feet long, but its proportions were far different from those of a modern salamander. Rather than having a long, slender body, it was unusually broad and flattened, with a distinctive disc-shaped form.
paragraphs.zh: 海生格罗托拉克斯（Gerrothorax maritimus）体长近三英尺，但其身体比例与现代蝾螈相差甚远。它并非拥有细长的身体，而是异常宽大扁平，呈现出独特的圆盘状形态。

paragraphs.en: "If you think about today's amphibians, this animal is unusual because it's big," Motani said. "It's probably, body mass-wise, about the same as the giant salamander, but what's different is that giant salamanders are elongated whereas this animal is really chunky."
paragraphs.zh: “如果你想想今天的两栖动物，这种动物之所以不寻常，是因为它很大，”元井说。“按体重来说，它可能和巨型蝾螈差不多，但不同之处在于，巨型蝾螈是细长的，而这种动物非常粗壮。”

paragraphs.en: The structure of its skull, together with its heavy armor, suggests that this ancient amphibian was an ambush predator. Instead of actively chasing its meals, it likely rested on the seafloor until an unsuspecting animal came within reach.
paragraphs.zh: 其头骨结构连同厚重的甲壳表明，这种远古两栖动物是一种伏击型捕食者。它可能不会主动追逐猎物，而是静卧在海底，直到毫无防备的动物进入攻击范围。

paragraphs.en: "They would probably just wait at the bottom and then when prey comes around, they would just suck it in," said Motani, who noted that the hunting strategy resembles that of the wobbegong, a type of carpet shark that lives near the seafloor and captures prey using suction.
paragraphs.zh: “它们可能只是待在底部等待，当猎物靠近时，就把猎物吸进去，”元井说。他指出，这种捕猎策略类似于须鲨（wobbegong），一种生活在海底附近、利用吸力捕获猎物的地毯鲨。

paragraphs.en: The problem comes down largely to amphibian skin. Unlike the relatively waterproof skin of many other animals, amphibian skin allows water and gases to pass through it. This makes it useful for breathing and maintaining hydration, but also leaves amphibians especially vulnerable to the effects of salt water.
paragraphs.zh: 问题主要出在两栖动物的皮肤上。与许多其他动物相对防水的皮肤不同，两栖动物的皮肤允许水和气体透过。这使其有助于呼吸和保持水分，但也使两栖动物特别容易受到海水的影响。
